WHAT BATCH 140 GUARANTEES ABOUT AN AUDIT RECORD, AND AGAINST WHOM -- recorded here because a security control stated without its limit is the overclaim this repository keeps removing. AGAINST THE SUBJECT OF THE RECORD acting as `authenticated`: guaranteed, at the privilege layer. No client role holds SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on app.audit_logs or app.security_events, so a member can neither forge a record about themselves nor edit nor remove one, and the refusal is 42501 before row level security is consulted. AGAINST `app_worker`: guaranteed for UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE. **AGAINST A ROLE THAT BYPASSES ROW LEVEL SECURITY: NOT GUARANTEED, AND FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY BUYS NOTHING.** `postgres` owns every table in `app` and holds BYPASSRLS (RFC-2026-021 §2/M2, and scripts/db/run.mjs's KNOWN_BYPASS pins the set), and BYPASSRLS beats FORCE -- forcing makes the OWNER subject to policies, and a bypassing role is outside the row-security system whether or not it owns the table. The owner can also disable RLS, drop a policy, grant itself a verb, delete, truncate and drop the table.

WHAT IS DONE ABOUT IT, AND WHAT IS NOT. §8.5's rule for an immutable table is "no user update/delete policy AND a command/trigger/privilege defense as appropriate"; batches 020, 030 and 040 took the privilege half, and 140 is the first table where the trigger half is appropriate, because it is the first whose adversary can hold the privilege. private.refuse_mutation() raises SQLSTATE ZZ140 on UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE for every role including the owner, and 140_audit.sql PROVES it by execution at apply time rather than citing it (RFC-2026-020 §6.2's rule): it writes a probe row as the migration role -- which owns the table and bypasses RLS -- requires all three verbs to raise, and rolls the probe back. **ITS LIMIT: the owner can `alter table ... disable trigger all` and then delete whatever it likes.** This is tamper RESISTANCE, not tamper EVIDENCE. It raises the cost from one statement to two and makes the first an act nobody performs by accident; a determined owner is not stopped and nothing in a database can stop one. Tamper evidence against that adversary is a hash chain, an append-only store outside this database, or WORM storage -- and CTR-AUD-001's freeze boundary lists "the audit STORE, its append-only or immutability mechanism, and any tamper evidence" as OPEN, with its untestable_by_schema note saying there is no hash chain field "because no source specifies one". This batch does not invent one. **Owed to A1 Security and to whoever freezes CTR-AUD-001.**

app.billing_invoices.provider_revision IS THE ORDERING §8.4 REQUIRES AND NOTHING ENFORCES ITS MONOTONICITY. §8.4: "Event type ไม่ใช่คำสั่งให้ set state แบบ blind", "ก่อนลดสิทธิ์หรือกรณี event เก่ากว่า projection ให้ fetch Subscription/Invoice ล่าสุดจาก Stripe", and "เก็บ provider_created_at, processed_at, provider object ID และ projection revision". BATCH 131 ADDS A UNIQUE CONSTRAINT TO A MERGED TABLE AS A FORWARD FIX, AND THE ROLLOUT CLAUSE INVARIANT 3 REQUIRES IS PAID ONLY FOR AN EMPTY TABLE. `alter table app.billing_subscriptions add constraint billing_subscriptions_workspace_key unique (workspace_id, id)` is needed because §3.3 requires a child of a tenant parent to take a composite foreign key, §4 invariant 10 states the failure it prevents, and batch 130's PARTIAL unique index cannot be a foreign key target. It is a forward fix and not a rewrite -- 130_billing.sql is not edited -- and migration invariant 3's `lock_timeout`, `statement_timeout`, rollout and recovery are all written into the file. THE LIMIT IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: `ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE` takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and builds an index, which is instantaneous only because app.billing_subscriptions is empty on every instance this batch can reach. On a populated instance the non-blocking path is invariant 4's -- `create unique index concurrently` outside a transaction, then `add constraint ... using index` -- which scripts/db/run.mjs does not support. §8.3's INBOX STATE MACHINE HAS FIVE STATES AND app.billing_webhook_receipts STORES NO STATUS COLUMN, WHICH IS THIS BATCH'S ONE DEPARTURE FROM A DIAGRAM A DOCUMENT ACTUALLY CONTAINS. RECEIVED, PROCESSED, RETRYABLE and DEAD_LETTER are the presence or absence of `processed_at`, `dead_lettered_at` and `next_attempt_at`; the fifth, PROCESSING, is distinguishable from RECEIVED only by a LEASE, which is `app.jobs`' lease_owner/lease_expires_at pair and which batch 050 owns. A status column would therefore be a second source of truth for three states and an invented vocabulary for the fourth, and CTR-JOB-001's freeze boundary -- "lifecycle state names and transition policy remain subject to source-defined owner review" -- is the sentence 050 refused twice on. The cost is that a processor cannot mark a receipt IN PROGRESS through this schema, so two workers claiming one receipt is not refused by anything here. §6's MIGRATION OWNERSHIP REGISTRY GIVES BATCH 070 THREE WORDS -- "research/evidence/suggestion" -- AND §5's INVENTORY NAMES FIVE OBJECTS, OF WHICH ONE IS IN NEITHER THE REGISTRY NOR §4's ERD. `research.core` is "runs/sources/snapshots/evidence/suggestions"; §4 draws RESEARCH_RUN, RESEARCH_SOURCE, EVIDENCE_ITEM and RESEARCH_SUGGESTION and no snapshot entity at all. Owed to A0 and to whoever amends the registry and the ERD.

§8.2 GIVES RESEARCH TWO ROWS THAT LOOK LIKE A CONTRADICTION AND ARE NOT, AND ONLY HALF OF THE FIRST CAN BE IMPLEMENTED. Starting research is therefore a COMMAND, RFC-2026-012 §4 names the mechanism (a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by app_command) and RFC-2026-021 §10 records that none exists, so a `Y` cell the matrix grants unconditionally to three roles has no path at all. This is the sharpest form the missing-command-surface debt has taken in this package: earlier batches recorded cells they could not reach because a VIEW was missing or a capability set was undefined; this one is a plain write that a person is entitled to make and cannot. DATA-DEC-07 ("Research snapshot retention, 30 วัน max default, owner Research+Legal, ก่อน real research source") IS OPEN, AND BATCH 070 ENCODES NOTHING, WHICH LEAVES A REAL GAP NAMED HERE RATHER THAN CLOSED. What the schema does is make the decision's absence structural rather than assumed: `app.research_snapshots.retention_until` is NOT NULL with NO DEFAULT and no arithmetic anywhere in the migration, so every capture states its own limit and none inherits a number nobody approved; it is outside every UPDATE grant to every role, so no granted path can push a stated limit forward; the apply-time block refuses a default (read from pg_attribute.atthasdef) and refuses an interval in any CHECK on the five tables; and `purged_at` beside it makes "this repository is holding captured material past its own stated limit" the query `purged_at is null and retention_until < now()` rather than a guess. WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS EVERYTHING THAT ACTS ON THAT: there is no sweep (batch 160 owns it), no source-policy mechanism (§10 says the real value is "สั้นกว่าตาม source policy" and nothing in this repository holds a source policy), and no legal-hold table (§10's retention precedence puts a hold first and defines it as hold_type, scope, reason code, created_by, approved_by, start/end/review date and an audit trail -- a subsystem, not a column). app.research_sources IS DECLARED APPEND-ONLY ON BATCH 070's OWN READING RATHER THAN ON A QUOTATION, AND A REVIEWER SHOULD PRESS ON IT. §5's mutability column for research.core reads "mixed; evidence immutable" -- it names ONE of five objects, and the other four are decisions the batch had to make. THERE IS NO CONTRACT FOR RESEARCH IN THE CONTRACT CATALOG, WHICH CHANGES WHAT A BOUND IN THIS SCHEMA CAN MEAN. `contract-catalog/` holds CTR-JOB-001, CTR-EVT-001, CTR-USG-001, CTR-NTF-001, CTR-AUD-001, CTR-TEN-001, CTR-IDM-001 and the rest, and no CTR-RES-*: batches 050, 051, 061, 131 and 140 could each derive their columns from a frozen envelope and declare their divergences from it, and batch 070 cannot.
